{
  "candidate_id": "issue117-geometry-hyp001",
  "behavior_problem_id": "issue117-behavior-first",
  "behavior_evidence_sha256": "793d52dce39a5a8aa3963ff566ae50612114b9d20d31227dfed3d1e9fc653b9b",
  "literature_evidence_sha256": "f44bfc70f57e7f993b30e1c15fa13157f2926ec29444a72e9f3afe33a08d4ce5",
  "next_item_hypothesis": "A demonstrated failure mode is that a flat, content-reconstruction-oriented SID can spend its coarse first token on broad semantic similarity while failing to group items with strongly directional train-split successor relations. In particular, train transitions include asymmetric high-count pairs such as 6574->9609 (37 observations) without a listed reverse edge, as well as 18674->19741 (33); the aggregate evidence reports 92.66% of directed pairs without an observed reverse. Hypothesis: negative-curvature residual quantization will make the coarse partition more efficient for nested, branching successor structure and increase first-token positive-hit behavior on the frozen validation pair construction. This is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated causal result; the evidence does not establish that curvature improves prediction.",
  "math_definition": {
    "mechanism": "Single geometry-controlled residual vector quantizer. The existing Stage2 content encoder and 32-dimensional latent projection produce z_i in R^32 for each item i. Three trainable codebooks C_l in R^(256x32) quantize a shared, recursively residualized latent. At each level, the level input is mapped to the curvature space, projected into the common bounded ball, assigned to the nearest projected code vector under the scored squared distance, and then the selected code vector is subtracted in tangent coordinates. The resulting three indices (k_i1,k_i2,k_i3) are the item's one global SID, used unchanged for every user and occurrence. No user, history, candidate list, beam search, or recommendation ranker is present in Stage2.",
    "curvature_constants": {
      "c": 0.1,
      "tau": 1e-6,
      "epsilon": 0.001,
      "projection_radius_R": 0.9,
      "flat_arm_c": 0.0,
      "domain_policy": "All tangent inputs are finite real 32-vectors. Map with the stated exp map, then radially project every point that will enter a distance, including every mapped residual and every mapped code vector, onto the closed ball of radius R. The same projection and R apply in both arms. Non-finite inputs or parameters fail the batch explicitly; they are not silently clipped. The arcosh argument is clamped below by 1+tau for numerical stability. At c=0, use the continuous flat-limit formulas: exp_0 is identity; the projection radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined and is not used; instead apply the same fixed-radius R projection. The scored distance is explicitly defined at c=0 by its exact limit. The common bounded feasible region and representation map therefore remain identical between arms.",
      "exp_map": "For c>0, Exp^c_0(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)*||v||), with value 0 at ||v||=0; at c=0, Exp^0_0(v)=v.",
      "projection": "P_R(x)=x*min(1,R/max(||x||,tau)); apply this after the exp map and before every distance evaluation. This fixed R projection is used for both arms and all mapped residual/code vectors.",
      "scored_squared_distance": "For c>0, D_c^2(x,y)=d_c(x,y)^2=(1/c)*arcosh(1+2*c*||x-y||^2/((1-c*||x||^2)*(1-c*||y||^2)))^2, where arcosh(u)=log(u+sqrt(max(u-1,0))*sqrt(u+1)) and its input is clamped to at least 1+tau. At c=0 define D_0^2(x,y)=4*||x-y||^2 exactly. The unsquared distance tends to 2*||x-y||, not 4*||x-y||^2. Both arms optimize the squared power D^2.",
      "c_dependent_rules_flat_limits": "The c-dependent representation rule Exp^c_0 tends to the identity at c->0. The c-dependent scored squared distance tends exactly to 4*||x-y||^2 at c->0 (and the unsquared distance tends to 2*||x-y||). The Poincare-ball radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined at c=0, so neither arm uses that radius: both use the identical fixed R projection. No other c-dependent assignment, loss, target, or update rule is used; c enters only through Exp^c_0 and D_c^2.",
      "residual_operation_order": "For item i and level l, with tangent residual r_i,l, first map u_i,l=Exp^c_0(r_i,l); second project x_i,l=P_R(u_i,l); for each code j map Exp^c_0(C_l[j]) and project q_l,j=P_R(Exp^c_0(C_l[j])); third assign k_i,l=argmin_j D_c^2(x_i,l,q_l,j), breaking exact ties by smallest j; fourth subtract in tangent coordinates r_i,l+1=r_i,l-C_l[k_i,l]. Thus the residual update is subtract-after-assignment, and its next-level mapped residual is projected before it is scored. Initialize r_i,1=z_i. The final global SID is the ordered tuple of the three assigned indices.",
      "conditioning": "Level 1 conditions on no earlier codes. Level 2 residual assignment conditions exactly on earlier code k1 through its residual update. Level 3 conditions exactly on earlier codes (k1,k2) through its residual update; no other codes or context condition an assignment.",
      "parameters_and_protocol": "Curved and flat arms are the same implementation with c as the sole geometry parameter, with identical architecture, trainable parameter count, initialization, optimizer, frozen epochs, batch size, learning-rate schedule, seeds, and training budget. No sweep or additional training protocol is introduced. Existing Stage2 frozen protocol values and codebook initialization are retained unchanged; this candidate does not alter or invent them. The content encoder/latent projection, when trainable under the frozen Stage2 protocol, is identically trained in both arms. The flat arm is the c->0 code path of the same implementation. There is no graph arm in this candidate. Stage2 does not rank items; downstream T5 Stage3 performs next-item ranking."
    },
    "loss_and_targets": {
      "named_tensors_and_shapes": "Let B be the frozen Stage2 training minibatch of item-content examples, n=|B|, z in R^(n x 32) the latent outputs, C_l in R^(256 x 32) the codebook at level l, k in {1,...,n}x{1,2,3} the assigned integer indices, and x_i,l and q_l,j in the projected ball as defined above. Let xhat_i be the decoder reconstruction of item i's content-feature vector a_i in R^F. Reduction means arithmetic mean over the explicitly named index set and feature coordinates where specified.",
      "reconstruction_objective": "L_rec=(1/(nF))*sum_{i=1}^n sum_{f=1}^F (xhat_{i,f}-a_{i,f})^2; reconstruction targets are the fixed item content features a_i, normalized only by nF, and if n=0 the minibatch is skipped with no optimizer update.",
      "quantization_objective": "For level l let sg denote stop-gradient and let r_i,l be the tangent residual before that level. Using x_i,l=P_R(Exp^c_0(r_i,l)) and q_l,k=P_R(Exp^c_0(C_l[k])), define L_commit=(1/(3n*32))*sum_{i=1}^n sum_{l=1}^3 ||sg[x_i,l]-q_l,k_i,l||_2^2 and L_codebook=(1/(3n*32))*sum_{i=1}^n sum_{l=1}^3 ||x_i,l-sg[q_l,k_i,l]||_2^2; both use the same D_c^2 geometry as assignment? No: these tangent/codebook fitting terms are replaced by the single geometry-consistent scored term L_q=(1/(3n))*sum_{i=1}^n sum_{l=1}^3 D_c^2(x_i,l,q_l,k_i,l). Only L_q is optimized for quantization; no separate Euclidean commitment or codebook fitting loss is added. If n=0, skip the minibatch without update.",
      "total_loss": "L=L_rec+L_q. Both terms are scalar means over their declared non-empty index sets; an empty batch is skipped. No train-transition target distribution is used in the loss: train transitions are permitted supervision, but this frozen mechanism is content reconstruction plus geometry-controlled quantization and avoids introducing a changed training protocol or transition-loss coefficient.",
      "parameter_dependent_targets": "The quantization indices k are discrete argmin assignments computed from the current parameters, treated as constants during each gradient evaluation (stop-gradient through assignment); gradients flow through selected distance operands and the stated objective, not through the argmin. Reconstruction targets a_i are fixed content features and do not depend on model parameters. No target distribution depends on trainable parameters, so no target/parameter circularity exists."
    }
  },
  "hyperbolic_necessity": "The relevant structural hypothesis is nested branching with directional, non-reciprocal successor relations: one coarse region may need to retain a shared semantic trunk while allocating progressively finer distinctions among divergent successors. Negative curvature is a plausible geometry for representing hierarchical branching with less distortion than a flat space, motivating its test in residual code assignment. The observed asymmetry and high-entropy transitions are only a trigger for this hypothesis, not proof that the transition graph is a tree, that the listed edges are causally meaningful, or that hyperbolic geometry is necessary. Necessity is operational and falsifiable here: under the identical bounded representation map and protocol, curvature should improve the registered SID diagnostics and downstream test metric over the exact flat limit.",
  "euclidean_control": "The control is the same model, bounded representation, codebooks, initialization, optimizer, schedule, seeds, training budget, losses and update ordering, with c=0 in the same code path. Stage2 produces only the stable global item SID. T5 Stage3 alone evaluates next-item ranking.",
  "real_trigger_measurement": "The trigger is the frozen train-only behavior manifest: 323633 distinct directed transition pairs, 24556 distinct items, mean next-item entropy 4.844072338042215 bits, and no observed reverse event for 314605 pairs (fraction 0.9266197178950221). These measurements motivate testing coarse-to-fine directional successor organization; they do not establish curvature benefit.   "training_only_inputs": "Stage2 may use only item content and the frozen train split, including train-split item transitions as permitted by CLAUDE.md rule 16; this candidate does not consume transition labels.     "latent_dim": 32,
    "levels": 3,
    "codes_per_level": 256,
    "hyperparameter_sweep": false,
    "uses_future_events": false
  },
  "stage2_diagnostic_definitions": {
    "valid_L1_positive_hit_rate": "Over the 52855 frozen validation pairs (one positive and ten negatives per anchor, seed 42, history[-1]->target), share for which anchor item's first SID token equals the positive item's first token.",
    "valid_Hard_L1_ER": "10*positive_hits/negative_hits, with negative_hits counted identically over the ten negatives; Resample reference is 16.38953942232631.",
    "level2_distinct_prefixes": "|{(k1,k2)}| over all items; reference 16145.",
    "L3_collision": "Share of items whose (k1,k2,k3) is shared with at least one other item.",
    "L3_refinement_gain": "Mean over items of log2(|bucket(k1,k2)|/|bucket(k1,k2,k3)|).",
    "conditional_G3": "Mean over the validation pairs of log2(p_hist(L3 target|anchor)/p_pref(L3 target|target prefix2)), with the train-transition history term mixed into a Laplace-smoothed (alpha=1 over 256 codes) prefix prior. This is diagnostic only, not a training target."
  },
  "falsifier": {
    "stage2_diagnostics": [
      {
        "name": "valid_L1_positive_hit_rate",
        "direction": "increase versus the paired flat arm",
        "minimum_effect": 0.005,
        "seed_rule": "For every frozen paired seed, compute curved minus flat on the exact fixed validation pairs; register the seed-wise difference and the arithmetic mean across seeds. Undefined or non-finite values follow NULL outcome rule."
      },
      {
        "name": "valid_Hard_L1_ER",

        "minimum_effect": 0.05,
        "seed_rule": "For every frozen paired seed, compute curved minus flat using the fixed numerator and denominator definition; register the seed-wise difference and arithmetic mean. A zero negative_hits denominator is NULL."
      },
      {
        "name": "level2_distinct_prefixes",
        "direction": "increase versus the paired flat arm",
        "minimum_effect": 100,
        "seed_rule": "For every frozen paired seed, compute curved minus flat across all items; register the seed-wise difference and arithmetic mean."
      },
      {
        "name": "L3_collision",
        "direction": "decrease versus the paired flat arm",
        "minimum_effect": 0.005,
        "seed_rule": "For every frozen paired seed, compute flat minus curved collision share across all items; register the seed-wise difference and arithmetic mean."
      },
      {
        "name": "L3_refinement_gain",
        "direction": "increase versus the paired flat arm",
        "minimum_effect": 0.05,
        "seed_rule": "For every frozen paired seed, compute curved minus flat over all items; register the seed-wise difference and arithmetic mean. Empty buckets or non-finite results are NULL."
      },
      {
        "name": "conditional_G3",
        "direction": "increase versus the paired flat arm",
        "minimum_effect": 0.02,
        "seed_rule": "For every frozen paired seed, compute curved minus flat on the exact frozen validation pairs and train-transition-smoothed prefix prior; register the seed-wise difference and arithmetic mean. Zero probabilities, empty strata, or non-finite values are NULL."
      }
    ],
    "stage3_behavioral_test": {
      "metric": "test_R@10",
      "direction": "increase versus the paired flat arm",
      "minimum_effect": 0.005,
      "seed_rule": "Evaluate downstream T5 Stage3 once per frozen paired seed using the unchanged test protocol; register curved minus flat test_R@10 seed-wise and its arithmetic mean. Stage3 test results are used only for this final test and never for tuning or Stage2 decisions."
    },
    "classification": {
      "falsified_if": "At least one registered non-NULL stage2 diagnostic aggregate is at or below its registered minimum_effect in the required direction, OR the registered non-NULL stage3_behavioral_test aggregate is at or below its registered minimum_effect in the required direction.",
      "passed_if": "Every registered stage2 diagnostic aggregate is non-NULL and at or above its registered minimum_effect in the required direction AND the registered stage3_behavioral_test aggregate is non-NULL and at or above its registered minimum_effect in the required direction.",
      "mixed_if": "At least one registered non-NULL comparison is at or above its registered minimum_effect in the required direction and at least one registered non-NULL comparison is below its registered minimum_effect in the required direction, with no NULL seed in any comparison required for classification; otherwise a NULL result is inconclusive and is neither passed nor falsified."
    },
    "null_outcome_rule": "If a seed-wise or aggregated change is undefined or non-finite (including zero denominator, missing evaluation, or empty stratum), classify that result NULL. A comparison with any NULL seed is inconclusive rather than passed or falsified; do not impute or drop the NULL seed."
  }
}
EOF
